Title: Bill Generation module (vendor/expense bills: Draft -> Pending Approval -> Approved -> Paid)
Objective: Implement src/bills/ as a simpler, single-approver-tier vendor/expense bill workflow distinct from the existing richer Expense/ExpenseApproval/ExpensePayment domain (multi-band configurable approval policies) and from ContributionBill (which bills donors, not vendors). Covers: Draft/edit, submit, approve (with mandatory creator-cannot-approve-own-bill defense-in-depth), reject-to-Draft with mandatory reason, mark-paid recording disbursement mode with a Ledger port hook (finance/ledger module doesn't exist yet -- Noop stub), cancel as the only correction path for a Paid bill, atomic sequential billNumber per organizationId+festivalYear via the existing SequenceCounterService, and a pure read-only OCR pre-fill hook (BillOcrPort) that proposes field values from a bill photo without ever auto-submitting.
Dependencies: P0-003 (Vendor/PaymentMode already in Prisma schema), P1-000 (PermissionGuard/TenantGuard, bill.create/bill.approve/bill.pay permission codes already seeded on Treasurer/Trust President/Secretary/Vice President default roles), P5-001 (Payments -- establishes the FestivalYearService + SequenceCounterService reuse pattern this module follows)
Acceptance Criteria: State machine structurally prevents any transition that skips a required step (Draft->Paid, Draft->Approved, Pending Approval->Paid all rejected by bill-state-machine.ts, not just by convention); billNumber is unique per organizationId+festivalYear and gapless under concurrent creation (reuses the same atomic SequenceCounterService proven in Receipts); approve() rejects when approvingUserId === bill.createdByUserId even when that user holds bill.approve (the seeded Treasurer role holds both bill.create and bill.approve, so this is a real, not hypothetical, misconfiguration this module must defend against); reject() returns status to Draft (per the endpoint's own '-> Draft' contract, reconciled against a data-model spec that also listed a Rejected enum value -- kept in the schema for fidelity but never assigned) with a mandatory reason preserved on rejectionReason and in BillAuditEvent; PATCH /bills/:id only succeeds while Draft, so a Paid bill's amount can never be edited directly, only /cancel can change its status thereafter; markPaid calls LedgerPort.recordBillPayment once, after the status write succeeds; every route requires bill.create and/or bill.approve/bill.pay -- a Volunteer-shaped permission set (neither) gets 403 on all 9 routes; requireOwnedBill (organizationId equality fetch-then-compare) blocks cross-tenant access even with a guessed id.
Tests: apps/api/src/bills/bill-number.formatter.spec.ts (3 tests); apps/api/src/bills/bill-state-machine.spec.ts (8 tests: full happy path, every skip-a-step rejection, cancel from every non-terminal status, terminal Cancelled/Paid guards); apps/api/src/bills/bills.service.spec.ts (16 tests: numbering, optional-field omission, service-level state machine skip rejections, CRITICAL self-approval regression, reject-to-Draft + resubmit, OCR pre-fill never touching a bill row, Paid immutability + cancel-only correction with Ledger hook assertion, cross-tenant isolation on get/approve/list); apps/api/src/bills/bills.controller.spec.ts (5 tests, including a loop asserting 403 across all 9 routes for a Volunteer-shaped permission set). Ran via `npx jest --config jest.config.js apps/api/src/bills`: Test Suites 4 passed, Tests 31 passed, 0 failed. Full repo regression: `npx jest --config jest.config.js`: Test Suites 23 passed, Tests 152 passed, 0 failed.
Security: bill.create/bill.approve/bill.pay are the only permission codes gating mutation routes, resolved server-side from roleId via PermissionResolutionService, never trusted from the client. GET /bills and GET /bills/:id use the OR-permission array support added to PermissionGuard during the Receipts task (bill.create or bill.approve, either suffices). Self-approval is blocked at the service layer by comparing createdByUserId against the approving userId directly -- explicitly not just relying on the permission check, since the current seeded Treasurer role holds both bill.create and bill.approve simultaneously. requireOwnedBill fetch-then-compare prevents cross-tenant reads/writes even with a valid but foreign bill id.

Bill.amount is Decimal(12,2), matching the same pre-existing paise-rule deviation already flagged in Payment.amount and PaymentReceipt.amountSnapshot -- not introduced fresh here, just kept consistent with the two prior modules.
